# Grilling

The interview primitive behind brainstorming, design, triage and coaching.

## Rules

- **Facts are your job, decisions are the user's.** Look up anything the code, docs, glossary, ADRs or `docs/inputs/` can answer. Ask only what needs a human decision.
- **One round at a time.** Ask three to five questions per round, numbered, each with your recommended answer and one line on why. The user can accept with "yes to all".
- **Walk the decision tree.** Track the open questions (the frontier). Each answer may open new branches; keep going until none are left.
- **Use the project's words.** Read `GLOSSARY.md`. When the user uses a fuzzy or conflicting term, stop and settle it.
- **Name trade-offs plainly.** For each real choice give the options and what each costs.
- **Stop when done.** Say "No open questions left" and summarise the decisions in a short list.

## Output

A list of resolved decisions, the terms that were sharpened, and any decision that is hard to reverse (a candidate ADR).
